land.text: all of Joseon: the Korean Empire was 'proclaimed in October 1897 by King Gojong of the Joseon dynasty'; infobox predecessor Joseon

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Korean Empire row starts in 1898, the Joseon row ends in 1897.

land.text: the whole of Korea: 'complete and permanent cession to His Majesty the Emperor of Japan of all rights of sovereignty over the whole of Korea' (Article 1)

successors.note: The infobox lists Chōsen and the Empire of Japan as successors; Chōsen (Korea under Japanese rule) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier on 18 October 2026. The annexation treaty was signed on 22 August 1910 and took effect on 29 August 1910.

capitals.name: Hanseong (Seoul)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Hanseong (present-day Seoul); Gojong was crowned at Hwangudan in the city. The page does not use the name Hwangseong.

rulers.name: Gojong (Yi Jae-hwang / Yi Hui)
rulers.title: emperor
rulers.note: Forced to abdicate on 19 July 1907 (page); the Joseon page counted him king from 1864.

rulers.name: Sunjong (Yi Cheok)
rulers.title: emperor
rulers.note: Succeeded on 19 July 1907; the treaty of annexation (22 August 1910) was signed for him by Ye Wanyong, the page says he 'refused to sign the treaty as required under Korean law'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1898 but the infobox dates the proclamation to 13 October 1897, so the 1898 outline is used for 1897. The page gives no area figure (only a map caption 'Territory of the Korean Empire 1903-1905'), so the 231,753 km2 of the Cliopatria shape could not be compared.
231,753 km2, the same outline as the last Joseon shape (1895-1897): the empire took over the whole kingdom, which the Joseon page puts on the Amnok and Tuman rivers. The page gives no area.
231,658 km2: the same outline within one edge cell of 1898; no page dates a border change in 1900. Jiandao north of the Tumen, claimed by Korea in 1901-1909 (Jiandao page), is not in the shape.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1905 outline, unchanged, shown as a Japanese protectorate from 17 November 1905 (status only)

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (231,753 km2), status changed: the Eulsa Treaty of 17 November 1905 'deprived Korea of its diplomatic sovereignty' and made it 'a protectorate of Imperial Japan', and the Residency-General opened in February 1906. Drawn as a Japanese vassal tint from November 1905; the empire-of-japan dossier carries the matching vassal_start (1905) and vassal_end (August 1910). Before that, Japanese forces occupied the country from February 1904 (ledger).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1908 outline, unchanged, a Japanese protectorate with its internal affairs under the Resident-General (status only)

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (231,753 km2), status the Japanese protectorate: the Japan-Korea Treaty of 1907 (signed on 24 July 1907 by Itō Hirobumi and Yi Wan-yong) 'transferred authority over Korea's internal affairs to the Resident-General' (Eulsa page), the army was disbanded on 1 August 1907 (Korean Empire page). Annexed on 29 August 1910.

region.text: the whole kingdom of Joseon, renamed the Daehan Empire

ledger.note: 1897: King Gojong proclaims the Korean Empire and is crowned emperor at Hwangudan. Infobox 'Empire proclaimed on 13 October 1897'; 'proclaimed in October 1897 by King Gojong of the Joseon dynasty'; named Daehan, regnal era Gwangmu.

region.text: Jiandao (Gando), the north bank of the Tumen River in Jilin (China side of the border only)

ledger.note: 1901: Korea sends police into Jiandao, the Tumen's north bank. 'Korea deployed police in Jiandao in 1901, continuing until 1906'; in 1903 the Korean government sent Yi Beom-yun as an observer. The page defines Jiandao as 'a historical border region along the north bank of the Tumen River in Jilin Province'; the region is a radius around Yanji, my reading of the Yanbian area.

region.text: Hanseong and the rest of Korea, occupied by Japanese forces

ledger.note: 1904: Japanese troops land at Incheon and occupy Hanseong, then the rest of Korea. 'From Incheon the Japanese occupied Hanseong and then the rest of Korea' (Russo-Japanese War page, infobox start 8 February 1904); Korean Empire page: 'Japanese troops marched through Seoul during the Russo-Japanese War in 1904'; the Eulsa page dates the Japan-Korea Protocol to 23 February 1904, under Japanese military presence, allowing Japan to 'occupy and use strategically important locations in Korea'. The empire-of-japan dossier does not carry this occupation.

region.text: Hanseong and the rest of Korea

ledger.note: 1905: the wartime occupation becomes the protectorate. Japan's occupation ended by no dated event on the pages opened; the Eulsa Treaty of 17 November 1905 'made Korea a protectorate of Imperial Japan' and the Treaty of Portsmouth (5 September 1905) 'recognized Japanese interests in Korea'. From November the empire-of-japan dossier draws Korea as a vassal tint; Japanese garrisons stayed (First Japan-Korea Agreement, 22 August 1904, 'allowed the creation of a Japanese garrison in Korea').

region.text: Jiandao (Gando), the north bank of the Tumen River in Jilin (China side of the border only)

ledger.note: 1909: the Gando Convention leaves Jiandao to China. Japan 'affirmed territorial rights of the Qing over Jiandao' and recognised the pre-invasion Tumen border; Japan had 'invaded Jiandao in August 1907' as Korea's protector. The page gives the year but not the month or the signatories.

1910: Korea is annexed by Japan. Signed on 22 August 1910 by Ye Wanyong and Terauchi Masatake; effective 29 August 1910; Article 1: 'complete and permanent cession to His Majesty the Emperor of Japan of all rights of sovereignty over the whole of Korea'. The empire-of-japan dossier records the matching gain.

region.text: the whole of Korea, annexed by Japan

ledger.note: 1910: the Korean Empire ends. Infobox 'Annexed by Japan: 29 August 1910'; 'After the Japan-Korea Treaty of 1910 was signed on 22 August 1910, the Korean Empire was annexed'.

wars.name: Russo-Japanese War

zones.text: Hanseong and the rest of Korea, occupied by Japan

wars.outcome: Japanese victory; the Treaty of Portsmouth (5 September 1905) 'recognized Japanese interests in Korea'; Korea, which had pursued a policy of neutrality, became a Japanese protectorate on 17 November 1905.
wars.note: Korea's neutrality was 'formally commended' by Russia, France, Germany and the United Kingdom on 27 January 1904 (Korean Empire page); the Battle of the Yalu River (1 May 1904) was fought on the border.

wars.name: Jiandao (Gando) border dispute

zones.text: Jiandao (Gando), the north bank of the Tumen River in Jilin (China side of the border only)

wars.outcome: Korean police entered Jiandao in 1901 and stayed to 1906; Japan 'invaded Jiandao in August 1907' as Korea's protector and in the 1909 Gando Convention 'affirmed territorial rights of the Qing over Jiandao'.
wars.note: Not a war: a contested border zone, listed because it feeds a contest event. Cliopatria's shapes stop at the Tumen (a few river-edge cells of China aside), so Jiandao proper is outside them.

certainty.note: The Yalu and Tumen boundary was set by the 1712 stele (Jiandao page) and is the empire's whole land frontier; the Jiandao shoal north of the Tumen was disputed until the 1909 Gando Convention and is the exception; the sea frontier is a coast.

notes: Cliopatria's four shapes are one outline (231,658-231,753 km2) and the dossier keeps them. The Wikipedia pages give no area for the empire (a map caption 'Territory of the Korean Empire 1903-1905' only), so no area comparison was possible. Protectorate: the Eulsa Treaty (17 November 1905) and the 1907 treaty make Korea a Japanese vassal; the suzerain owns the vassal events and the empire-of-japan dossier has vassal_start 1905 / vassal_end 1910 and the 1910 gain, so this dossier carries the keyframe status changes (verdict adjust, shape unchanged) and the matching loss in 1910 but not a vassal event. The wartime occupation 1904-1905 is recorded here (occupation_start/end with counterpart empire-of-japan) because the Japan dossier does not carry it; a rendering agent should check the overlap with its vassal tint in 1905. Not on the pages opened: the date the wartime occupation ended (1905, confidence 1 at the Eulsa Treaty); the dates of Jiandao's Korean administration beyond 'police in 1901-1906'; the signatories and month of the Gando Convention; the Russian frontier at the Tumen mouth (Cliopatria neighbour Russian Empire 1898-1910, no page opened), Qing neighbour contacts of 1898-1899 (the Joseon-Qing border is the Yalu-Tumen line; the Treaty of Shimonoseki, 17 April 1895, ended the Qing suzerainty, Joseon dossier). The qing-dynasty slug is used for the Jiandao contest and is a Cliopatria row (ea-08). Successor Chōsen (Korea under Japanese rule 1910-1945) has no row and no dossier: counterparts_needing_dossiers in the report. Page budget: five pages (Korean Empire, Eulsa Treaty, Japan-Korea Treaty of 1910, Russo-Japanese War, Jiandao); Jiandao was opened for the Joseon dossier and reused.
